subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & cost levers for Atlas Health pilot
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Diana Morris <diana.morris@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & cost levers for Atlas Health pilot

Thanks again for taking the time today, Diana — great conversation. This thread is a short recap + proposed next steps so we can scope the pilot and give you concrete cost estimates. I copied Sergio and Karthik from our infra/SE team so we can align on technical trade-offs.

Recap from our call:
- Primary goal: integrate Redwoods inference for clinical note summarization (near-real-time) into Atlas frontend.
- Key SLOs you mentioned: P95 latency target for response, acceptable tail latency, and support for streaming partial results in the UI.
- Expected load: baseline 150 qps during business hours, burst to ~900 qps for peak events; concurrency for a single model replica estimated at 32 concurrent sessions.

Open items for us to validate/size:
1) Exact P95 target: you said ~200–300ms, can you confirm desired P95 and P99?
2) Streaming: do you need token-level streaming (partial paragraphs) or chunked message updates?
3) Payload sizes: avg input tokens per request and max tokens per response (typical and worst-case).
4) Peak concurrency during multi-region failover or bulk processing windows.

Initial Redwood recommendations (high-level):
- If P95 <= 200ms: prefer a dedicated model variant + aggressive continuous batching + KV prefix caching to reduce per-token work.
- Streaming: use our streaming path with small chunk sizes (200–400ms flush) — that affects throughput but improves perceived latency.
- Cost levers: 4-bit quantized model variant for non-sensitive routes, model family fallback for heavy tails, and autoscale with burst capacity for predictable peak windows.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Diana/Atlas: confirm items (1)-(3) above and share a sample of representative payloads (PII redacted).
- Redwood: Sergio to run a quick micro-benchmark (with a representative payload) and return a playbook with estimated cost/throughput for the two SLO bands (P95 200ms vs 300ms).
- Schedule: can we target delivery of the micro-benchmark + playbook by EOD 2026-03-03?

Attachments: I attached a starter SLO matrix template (atlas_slo_matrix.xlsx) for you to fill — keeps the numbers consistent for sizing. Also attached a short perf playbook (redwood_perf_playbook.pdf) we’ll update after the benchmark.

Thanks — Camila

From: Diana Morris <diana.morris@atlashealth.com>

Cc: Atlas Health SRE <sre@atlashealth.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & cost levers for Atlas Health pilot

Thanks Camila — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers:
- Confirmed targets: P95 <= 250ms as target; P99 we care about but can tolerate up to 800ms for now. If the 250ms path is too costly, we can evaluate a 300ms SLO as fallback.
- Streaming: we want token-level streaming in the UI (user sees partial summary as it completes). Latency perceived is more important than total compute time.
- Payloads: avg input ~120 tokens; avg output target ~220 tokens; worst-case outputs ~800 tokens for long notes. Will attach a small sample set.
- Peaks: our telemetry shows baseline 120–180 qps; occasional peaks for heavy clinic hours up to ~850 qps sustained for ~10–15min.

I attached a zip of sample payloads (redacted). We need an estimate for both: (A) P95=250ms with token streaming, and (B) P95=300ms (cheaper) with same streaming UX. Also flag any data-surface impacts if you recommend quantized variants (we have to validate output quality clinically).

Diana
Diana Morris
Product Lead, Integrations — Atlas Health
diana.morris@atlashealth.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & cost levers for Atlas Health pilot

Perfect, thanks for the numbers and sample payloads — that helps a lot. Quick clarifications from our side:
- For token-level streaming with perceived latency <=250ms, we’ll likely need to prioritize a lower-latency model variant (reduced context switching) and keep batching windows tight (10–25ms). That increases CPU/GPU kernel overhead slightly vs larger batch windows.
- For the 800-token worst-case outputs: we’ll recommend an early-flush heuristic for streaming so the UI gets useful partials quickly; full completion can be allowed to take longer without impacting perceived SLO.

Next steps (confirmed):
- Sergio will run a micro-benchmark using your samples against two configs (P95=250ms optimized path vs P95=300ms cost-optimized path).
- Redwood to provide: perf numbers (p95/p99), estimated sustained cost per 1M tokens, recommended batching / cache settings, and expected model quality delta for 4-bit quantized variant.
- Proposed meeting to review results: Thu 2026-03-04 10:00 PT — does that work for your team?

Thanks — Camila

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Diana Morris <diana.morris@atlashealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & cost levers for Atlas Health pilot

Hey Diana / team — I ran a quick set of micro-benchmarks this morning using the sample payloads and two configurations. Below is a short technical summary (numbers are synthetic estimates for sizing; I’ll attach full logs if you want them).

Bench summary (representative single-replica numbers):
- Config A (low-latency path, P95 ≈ 240ms streaming):
  - Continuous batching window: 12ms
  - Concurrency per GPU: ~28 sessions (sustained)
  - Token throughput: ~9k tokens/s per GPU on A100 -> scales linearly with replicas
  - Typical p99 observed ~680ms with 800-token outputs
  - Cost estimate: ~1.8x relative to cost-optimized config for same QPS (higher due to tight batching and lower kernel amortization)

- Config B (cost-optimized path, P95 ≈ 300ms streaming):
  - Continuous batching window: 40ms
  - Concurrency per GPU: ~64 sessions
  - Token throughput: ~14k tokens/s per GPU
  - p99 observed ~920ms on worst-case outputs
  - Cost estimate: ~0.55x of Config A for same QPS

Recommended cost/perf levers to hit the 250ms SLO with reasonable cost:
1) Prefix/KV caching for repeated clinical templates — effective for ~20–35% token reduction in median workloads.
2) Mixed model strategy: primary low-latency variant for interactive UI; fallback to quantized variant (4-bit) for batch re-runs or non-critical endpoints. We should run a brief quality regression on your clinical outputs before recommending wide 4-bit use.
3) Autoscale policy with reserved baseline capacity + burst pool. Reserve enough replicas to handle baseline 200 qps with Config B and allow burst to Config A instances for short windows.
4) Streaming flush heuristic: emit partial responses every 200–300ms or on sentence boundaries to balance perceived latency and throughput.

Action items I'll deliver by EOD 2026-03-03:
- CSV with observed p50/p95/p99 for both configs (per-payload), plus GPU token/sec numbers.
- Draft playbook: recommended batching windows, cache TTLs, quantization candidates, expected cost deltas.

Notes on quality: initial diff tests on your sample set show minimal semantic drift for short outputs at 4-bit for ~70% of cases; for clinical accuracy we should run a small physician-led eval set.

I’ll upload logs and the playbook draft to the HubSpot deal and Drive links in this thread. If Thu 2026-03-04 10:00 PT still works, I’ll be on the call to walk through the numbers.

— Sergio
